methodologyNotes: Covers over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids sold directly to US consumers without a prescription or professional fitting, intended for adults with perceived mild-to-moderate hearing loss, at a published US price. Excludes prescription/audiologist-fit hearing aids, non-FDA personal sound amplification products (PSAPs), and cochlear implants. Price is typical direct US retail per PAIR in USD unless noted in priceNote. styleType is the wear style enum (CIC = completely-in-canal, ITC = in-the-canal, ITE = in-the-ear, RIC = receiver-in-canal, BTE = behind-the-ear). maxGainDb is maximum full-on acoustic gain in decibels; null if not disclosed. bluetoothStreaming is the audio-streaming support enum (none, iOS, Android, iOS+Android); 'none' means the device pairs for control only or not at all. selfFitting is a boolean: true if the device offers FDA self-fitting or an app-driven hearing test / audiogram-based tuning. rechargeable is a boolean (true = built-in rechargeable cell, false = replaceable disposable battery). batteryLifeHrs is rated wear time per full charge in hours (for disposable-battery models, rated hours per battery); null if not disclosed. waterResistanceIp is the ingress-protection rating string as published (e.g. 'IP68', 'IP54'); null if not disclosed. soundChannels is the number of sound-processing channels/bands as published; null if not disclosed. listeningPrograms is the count of selectable preset listening environments/programs; null if not disclosed. warrantyYears is the standard manufacturer warranty in years. trialPeriodDays is the risk-free return/trial window in days. weightPerAidGrams is the mass of a single aid in grams (excluding charging case); null if not disclosed.

products.name: Jabra Enhance Select 700
products.priceNote: Official Jabra Enhance product page lists "$1,995 ... per pair" (MSRP; "or as low as $65/mo per pair"). HearingTracker corroborates "$1,995 per pair" as MSRP, noting a current promo of $1,795/pair with a $200 coupon. priceUsd reflects the $1,995 per-pair MSRP.
products.provenance: The official Jabra Enhance product page (jabraenhance.com/product/enhanceselect700) confirms this exact model, "Enhance Select 700," at $1,995 per pair, with a per-aid weight of 2.12 grams, a rechargeable battery delivering 24-hour power on a full 3-hour charge, Bluetooth streaming to compatible Apple or Android devices, a 100-day risk-free trial, and a 3-year warranty. HearingTracker's dated Oct 28, 2025 review corroborates the same $1,995 per-pair MSRP and identifies it as the smallest receiver-in-canal (RIC) design, self-fitting via app/audiogram, with an IP68 rating, 12 adjustment bands, and 4 fully flexible programs. Both pages are unambiguously about this exact flagship model (the successor to the Select 500), not a sibling variant; maxGainDb was not disclosed on either page (only a 116 dB input dynamic range, which is not acoustic gain), so it is left null.

products.name: Audien Atom Pro 2

products.provenance: The Audien manufacturer page (audienhearing.com/products/atom-pro-2) confirms this exact model — "Audien Atom Pro 2 OTC Hearing Aids" with built-in UV-cleaning case, A2 chip, "4 different hearing modes," "up to 24 hours" battery, and a "45-Day Risk Free Trial" — priced at "just $289 /pair." HearingTracker's dated review (updated Feb 6, 2026) corroborates the model identity as the updated ITE/earbud-hybrid successor to the original Atom Pro (distinct from the newer Atom X flagship), sold on Audien and Amazon at "$289 per pair," and states it is lithium-ion rechargeable with 24-hour battery, four preset listening modes, no app/Bluetooth streaming, preset-only fitting (no self-fit/audiogram), and "Not Ingress Protection (IP) rated." Price and every filled spec are verbatim from these two fetched pages; maxGainDb, soundChannels, warrantyYears, weightPerAidGrams, and IP rating were not disclosed and are left null.
